title: Acid, salt and bitterness
subtitle: The elements that make wine softer
objectives: Explain why acidic food needs acidic wine

steps.title: Acid in the food
steps.body: Acidic food, like a tomato salad or a dish with lemon, makes a wine taste less acidic, richer and fruitier. But if the wine has lower acidity than the dish, it can taste flat and flabby. So acidic food needs a wine with at least as much acidity, like Sauvignon Blanc or Chianti.

steps.title: Salt and bitterness
steps.body: Salt makes wine feel softer and fruitier, which is why salty cheeses and charcuterie are so easy to pair. Bitterness works the other way: bitter food adds to bitterness in the wine. Grilled radicchio or very charred meat can make a tannic red taste harsh, because tannin itself tastes slightly bitter.

steps.prompt: Match each food element to its effect on wine.
steps.explanation: Salt and acidity soften a wine. Sweetness and bitterness harden it.

steps.body: Salty blue cheese with a sweet wine, like Roquefort with Sauternes, is one of the great pairings. Salt softens, sweetness balances salt, and the wine's acidity cuts the fat.

steps.prompt: A tomato salad with lemon dressing needs a wine with high ____.
steps.explanation: Acidic food makes a wine seem less acidic, so the wine needs plenty of acidity to stay fresh.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Acidic food needs wine with at least as much acidity
Salt is wine-friendly, softening and lifting fruit
Bitter food adds to the bitterness of tannic wines
